articles.title: With $720M round, Britain’s Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips
articles.snippet: With $720M round, Britain’s Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips TechCrunch
articles.text:
Fractile , a British startup developing AI chips, has raised a $720 million Series C backed by Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund with hopes of “ensuring the U.K. has a greater stake in the hardware that will underpin its future economy,” its government stated .
Alongside the likes of Axelera , Etched , and OLIX , this makes Fractile one of the top-funded startup players in the race for purpose-built AI chips. Such chips are one of several avenues being explored to reduce the cost of inference — aka using increasingly demanding AI models in production.
However, Fractile seeks to go beyond hardware with a full-stack approach that also includes a machine learning compiler to maximize the speed at which LLMs will get executed on its chips.
As a result, the company frames itself as a frontier AI company, and its latest round led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Redpoint was priced accordingly. According to the British government, the valuation was “over £5 billion” — quite possibly $7 billion, a figure reported both by the Financial Times and a Reuters source .
Still, Fractile’s main differentiator will arguably be its hardware design. After a pivot , its approach now revolves on DRAM, the most common type of RAM, but stacked on top of each chip in such a way that it is hoping will bypass the usual trade-off between memory and capacity.
This trade-off has become more problematic with the rise of agentic AI, as companies seek to perform longer chains of tasks with large models without compromising on speed. As compute struggles to keep up, hopes are high for AI chips, despite their limited availability to date.
In a LinkedIn post , Fractile CEO Walter Goodwin wrote that “there is still a lot of work ahead” for the company, and that the new funding will enable the startup to “ship [its] first chips and systems next year.”

articles.title: SoftBank-Led Agile Robots Raises $500M Series F at $8.5B Valuation
articles.snippet: SoftBank-Led Agile Robots Raises $500M Series F at $8.5B Valuation Wowtale
articles.text:
A German company that has deployed more than 20,000 industrial robot solutions now has a plant that can build up to 10,000 humanoids a year. Munich-based Physical AI company Agile Robots has raised a $500 million Series F led by SoftBank Group, valuing it at $8.5 billion and bringing total funding to $2 billion.
Agile Robots announced the round on Nov. 12. SoftBank Group led, with NVIDIA, Hitachi Group (Hitachi and Hitachi Ventures) and T.Capital among the participants. The company says the investors span the automotive, artificial intelligence, digital and industrial technology sectors. SoftBank is a longtime backer: its Vision Fund 2 led the company’s $220 million Series C in September 2021 at a valuation above $1 billion, so the new valuation is more than eight times that. According to Bloomberg, a round of about $800 million, with SoftBank anchoring more than $300 million, was under discussion in June, and the round closed smaller at $500 million. Hitachi Ventures also joined Graphon Labs’ $35 million Series A this month.
The company builds humanoid and mobile robots, robotic arms and hands, and the software and AI models behind them, aimed at automotive, consumer electronics, healthcare and service customers that want to automate tasks that have relied on human dexterity and judgment. It was founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and says it has deployed 20,000 industrial robotic solutions across automotive, consumer electronics, logistics and other industries. It has more than 3,500 employees from almost 60 countries, including more than 2,000 R&D experts, and over 650 patents, and develops and builds its hardware and software in-house from more than 20,000 square meters of lab space.
Founder and CEO Zhaopeng Chen said the company wants to bring Physical AI out of the lab and into industrial production across logistics, automotive, electronics and manufacturing. The money will go to global expansion, a stronger presence in key markets and more production capacity. Agile Robots plans to strengthen its presence in the United States and speed up development of new robotics applications, while continuing to build out production capacity, including in Germany. A new site opened early this year in Fürstenfeldbruck, near Munich, can produce up to 10,000 legged and wheeled humanoid robots a year. Dennis Chang, managing partner at SoftBank Investment Advisers, said Agile Robots combines deep robotics expertise with the ability to execute at industrial scale, and that SoftBank looks forward to continuing to partner with Chen’s team.
Acquisitions have widened the business. In November 2023 it took over the operations of insolvent Munich robotics company Franka Emika , which now runs as Franka Robotics and serves as an AI robotics research platform. Last November it announced the acquisition of thyssenkrupp’s Automation Engineering business , and in April it closed the deal . The unit now operates as industrial deployment specialist Krause Automation, and the company said at the time it would add about 650 experts and 10 locations in Europe and North America. BÄR Automation and Idealworks are also subsidiaries, and its humanoid lineup includes Agile ONE. The company has not disclosed revenue.

SoftBank Leads $500 Million Funding Round for Agile Robots in Germany
By: Asia Business Outlook Team | Thursday, 12 November 2026
Japanese investment group SoftBank has led a US$500 million funding round in German robotics company Agile Robots , valuing the company at US$8.5 billion.
The funding round also saw participation from semiconductor company Nvidia , Japanese technology firm Hitachi and T. Capital.
The investment comes as interest in artificial intelligence and robotics continues to grow, with more companies looking to use these technologies in manufacturing and other industries.
Agile Robots plans to use the funds to expand its business in the United States, increase production in Germany and develop new industrial applications.
The company is looking to benefit from the growing demand for automation technology across manufacturing, logistics and other sectors. The investment is also expected to help it strengthen its position in the global robotics market .
Key Highlights
SoftBank Leads $500 Million Funding Round in German Robotics Firm Agile Robots
Agile Robots Reaches $8.5 Billion Valuation After SoftBank-Led Investment
Nvidia and Hitachi Join SoftBank in $500 Million Investment in Agile Robots
SoftBank and Nvidia Support Agile Robots' Expansion
Founded in 2018 by researchers from the German Aerospace Center, Agile Robots develops robotic systems that combine artificial intelligence with advanced hardware. Its products include industrial robotic arms , robotic hands, autonomous transport systems and humanoid robots used for different industrial applications.
The company has more than 3,500 employees across over 25 locations worldwide. It also says that more than 20,000 of its automation solutions are currently in use globally. Agile Robots holds over 650 patents related to its technology.
With the latest investment, the company has raised approximately US$2 billion since its establishment. SoftBank had previously led a US$220 million Series C funding round in Agile Robots in 2021, helping it expand its operations.
Nvidia's participation is another important part of the deal. The chipmaker has been increasing its investments and partnerships in robotics as it looks to expand the use of AI beyond computers and data centres. This includes physical AI , which allows machines to understand their surroundings and carry out tasks in the real world.
Agile Robots has also partnered with Google DeepMind to improve the capabilities of its robotic systems. The collaboration is aimed at developing robots that can perform more complex tasks in industrial settings.
Company Plans to Increase Production in Germany
Agile Robots will use the new funding to expand its operations in the United States and increase its manufacturing capacity in Germany. It also plans to develop more applications for its robotic systems as manufacturers look for ways to improve productivity and reduce manual work.
Earlier this year, the company opened a manufacturing facility in Fürstenfeldbruck, near Munich. The facility is designed to produce up to 10,000 humanoid robots annually. This will help Agile Robots increase production and prepare for growing demand.
